title: The assembled specialist buy-back: oracle-routed vs code-routed vs confidence-gated vs the sealed dense ladder
question: The parts are sealed (M119/M124: per-domain super-additive at ~5.6x fewer MACs; M139a: code-routed domain dispatch at 75.6%). The assembled routed system was never run. Does the ASSEMBLED system - specialists dispatched by the code-router, no domain labels at inference - beat the sealed dense r28 arm per domain at ~2.4x fewer per-image MACs?

sparse.specialist_construction: A5-exact (M119/M124): global M108 whitener; per-domain candidate pool (n_cap 20000, seed [11, domain]) restricted to the domain's train rows; dictionary = candidates in the [11,100] seeded-permutation order, first 512 atoms; triangle encode on GPU with the registered throttle; closed-form ridge lambda=1.0.

sealed_codes.note: Global fallback + domain router fitted on the SEALED 6144-atom memmaps (dual accumulate, the M139a convention).

routing.tau_note: 0.2046 = the SEALED M139a router-margin q25 (logs/results/v16/m139a_routing_slack/evidence.json), registered BEFORE this run. gated(tau): router margin >= tau -> routed specialist, else the global head.

gate.kill_switch_buyback: fired if the ROUTED arm's per-domain accuracy beats the sealed dense r28 per-domain accuracy on fewer than 4 of 6 domains.
gate.consequence_fired: the assembled buy-back fails the A5 pattern; the negative is sealed and reported.
gate.consequence_passed: the assembled buy-back holds end-to-end: code-routed specialists beat dense r28 per domain on >= 4/6 domains at ~2.4x fewer MACs.
